About Me

I am passionate about building a career at the intersection of analog/mixed-signal IC design and silicon validation — bringing circuits from specification through bench bring-up and into reliable production. My work spans fully differential op-amps, RF front-ends, and SAR ADC design in IBM 180nm CMOS, and I complement that circuit-level depth with hands-on validation experience: automated test pipelines in Python, PVT corner and Monte Carlo analysis in Cadence Spectre, and UVM-based functional verification that has driven 100% coverage on real RTL. I am drawn to the full mixed-signal product lifecycle — translating silicon measurements into actionable design improvements, not just running simulations. Whether characterizing photonic devices in my research role or debugging system-level requirements during my time at Deloitte, I have always gravitated toward the intersection of rigorous analysis and practical problem-solving. My goal is to grow into a semiconductor engineer who owns design quality end-to-end: from first schematic to customer-facing validation.

Professional Summary

  • M.S. Electrical Engineering student at Texas A&M University (GPA 3.3/4.0), specializing in analog/mixed-signal IC design and silicon validation. Hands-on experience designing and characterizing fully differential op-amps, RF front-ends (2.4 GHz), and SAR ADCs at transistor level in IBM 180nm CMOS using Cadence Virtuoso and Spectre. Proficient in full design-cycle workflows spanning schematic, simulation, post-layout verification (DRC/LVS/PEX), and PVT corner/Monte Carlo analysis. Experienced in Python-automated bench validation pipelines and UVM-based functional verification (100% functional coverage) in SystemVerilog. Currently conducting silicon photonics research at TAMU, designing and characterizing integrated photonic devices (waveguides, directional couplers, resonators) using Lumerical FDTD and COMSOL. Seeking internship opportunities in analog/mixed-signal IC design, silicon validation, or RF IC engineering.
